get.description: Use for a connectivity check. The response has a top-level status field.
Use for introductory planet cards. The static list is ordered from Mercury through Neptune.

data.name: Mercury
data.summary: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the Sun.
data.funFact: A year on Mercury lasts just 88 Earth days.

data.name: Venus
data.summary: Venus is the hottest planet because its thick atmosphere traps heat.
data.funFact: On Venus, the Sun rises in the west because Venus spins the opposite way from Earth.

data.name: Earth
data.summary: Earth is our rocky home planet. Oceans cover most of its surface.
data.funFact: Earth takes about 365 days and 6 hours to travel once around the Sun.

data.name: Mars
data.summary: Mars is a rocky planet covered in rusty dust that makes it look red.
data.funFact: Mars has the largest volcano in the solar system. It is called Olympus Mons.

data.name: Jupiter
data.summary: Jupiter is the largest planet. Bands of clouds wrap around this gas giant.
data.funFact: Jupiter’s Great Red Spot is a giant spinning storm.

data.name: Saturn
data.summary: Saturn is a gas giant surrounded by bright rings.
data.funFact: The rings are made of billions of pieces of ice and rock.

data.name: Uranus
data.summary: Uranus is a very cold planet with faint rings.
data.funFact: Uranus spins on its side, like a ball rolling around the Sun.

data.name: Neptune
data.summary: Neptune is a cold, windy planet and the farthest from the Sun.
data.funFact: A year on Neptune lasts about 165 Earth years.

data.title: Reading the traces of hot water
data.summary: Near Mexicali, geothermal alteration offers a laboratory for asking how water changes rocks. Comparing these processes with ancient Martian evidence helps students investigate habitability without claiming identical conditions or life.

similarities.text: Water interacting with rock can modify mineral assemblages; alteration at both sites motivates testing competing formation mechanisms.

differences.text: Cerro Prieto is an active sediment-hosted geothermal system. Ancient Gusev alteration has competing interpretations; this is neither identical mineralogy nor a modern Mars environment.

Earth has a protective atmosphere, a different radiation environment, abundant biology and different weathering. Gravity, atmospheric pressure and composition, liquid-water stability, thermal cycles and geological timescales differ. Infrastructure also changes terrestrial sites.

data.priorityReason: Best local process study, with historical Earth mineralogical observations and rover alteration evidence; the pair itself remains a proposed analogy.

alternativeMatches.name: Gale silica-rich alteration
alternativeMatches.decision: Retained as an alternative: similar ambiguity, but Gusev provides the stronger hydrothermal-focused teaching case.

educational.headline: Reading the traces of hot water
educational.summary30: Near Mexicali, geothermal alteration offers a laboratory for asking how water changes rocks. Comparing these processes with ancient Martian evidence helps students investigate habitability without claiming identical conditions or life.
educational.explanation: Imagine choosing a rock that might preserve evidence of an old water system. You would first need to know what the rock looked like before it changed. Cerro Prieto gives researchers a place to investigate that question through altered sediments and geothermal observations. Spirit’s discoveries in Gusev raise related questions about ancient water on Mars. The useful connection is an investigative method: compare altered and less altered material, identify minerals, and test alternative explanations. A similar chemical signal can arise through different pathways. Students can design a sampling strategy and explain what result would challenge their preferred explanation. The comparison does not establish life on Mars, a shared mineral inventory, or equivalent modern surface conditions.
educational.youngExplorers: Could a changed rock tell a story about hot water? Near Mexicali, scientists can study such changes. On Mars, a rover found rocks that invite similar questions.
educational.students: An alteration mineral records a chemical reaction, not a complete environment. Compare altered material with its original rock and ask whether water added silica or removed other components.
educational.advanced: Proposed process analogy, not a published validation of this exact site pair. Compare primary host composition, alteration textures and fluid chemistry before computing overlap. The present release contains no paired assemblage measurements.

facts.text: Cerro Prieto research examined altered sediments near surface geothermal emissions.
Spirit found silica-rich materials near Home Plate.
Silica enrichment can have competing alteration explanations.

educational.whyItMatters: This comparison helps design a testable investigation. Best local process study, with historical Earth mineralogical observations and rover alteration evidence; the pair itself remains a proposed analogy.
educational.analogyBreakdown: Cerro Prieto is an active sediment-hosted geothermal system. Ancient Gusev alteration has competing interpretations; this is neither identical mineralogy nor a modern Mars environment. Earth has a protective atmosphere, a different radiation environment, abundant biology and different weathering. Gravity, atmospheric pressure and composition, liquid-water stability, thermal cycles and geological timescales differ. Infrastructure also changes terrestrial sites.

quiz.question: What does silica enrichment alone prove?
options: That microbes lived there
That the rock is identical to Cerro Prieto
Neither a unique formation mechanism nor life
That modern Mars has geothermal pools
quiz.explanation: Alternative reactions can enrich silica; independent context is needed.

experiment.title: Design an alteration transect
steps: Use permitted archived samples or published spectra; do not enter industrial geothermal areas.
Choose altered and background controls from the same host material.
Compare mineral identifications and record detection limits.
Test both leaching and precipitation hypotheses.
experiment.outcomeLabel: Educational scenario; not a real mission prediction
experiment.limitations: Cerro Prieto is an active sediment-hosted geothermal system. Ancient Gusev alteration has competing interpretations; this is neither identical mineralogy nor a modern Mars environment.

ranking.reason: Requires at least 70% weighted coverage and up to three measured dimensions. No missing value is treated as zero.
ranking.method: starman-distance-v1; heuristic thresholds, not scientific validation

data.title: Reading the traces of hot water
data.summary: Near Mexicali, geothermal alteration offers a laboratory for asking how water changes rocks. Comparing these processes with ancient Martian evidence helps students investigate habitability without claiming identical conditions or life.

data.scoringMethod: Unscored; proposed pair with no paired numerical observations

similarities.text: Water interacting with rock can modify mineral assemblages; alteration at both sites motivates testing competing formation mechanisms.

differences.text: Cerro Prieto is an active sediment-hosted geothermal system. Ancient Gusev alteration has competing interpretations; this is neither identical mineralogy nor a modern Mars environment.

Earth has a protective atmosphere, a different radiation environment, abundant biology and different weathering. Gravity, atmospheric pressure and composition, liquid-water stability, thermal cycles and geological timescales differ. Infrastructure also changes terrestrial sites.

data.priorityReason: Best local process study, with historical Earth mineralogical observations and rover alteration evidence; the pair itself remains a proposed analogy.

alternativeMatches.name: Gale silica-rich alteration
alternativeMatches.decision: Retained as an alternative: similar ambiguity, but Gusev provides the stronger hydrothermal-focused teaching case.

educational.headline: Reading the traces of hot water
educational.summary30: Near Mexicali, geothermal alteration offers a laboratory for asking how water changes rocks. Comparing these processes with ancient Martian evidence helps students investigate habitability without claiming identical conditions or life.
educational.explanation: Imagine choosing a rock that might preserve evidence of an old water system. You would first need to know what the rock looked like before it changed. Cerro Prieto gives researchers a place to investigate that question through altered sediments and geothermal observations. Spirit’s discoveries in Gusev raise related questions about ancient water on Mars. The useful connection is an investigative method: compare altered and less altered material, identify minerals, and test alternative explanations. A similar chemical signal can arise through different pathways. Students can design a sampling strategy and explain what result would challenge their preferred explanation. The comparison does not establish life on Mars, a shared mineral inventory, or equivalent modern surface conditions.
educational.youngExplorers: Could a changed rock tell a story about hot water? Near Mexicali, scientists can study such changes. On Mars, a rover found rocks that invite similar questions.
educational.students: An alteration mineral records a chemical reaction, not a complete environment. Compare altered material with its original rock and ask whether water added silica or removed other components.
educational.advanced: Proposed process analogy, not a published validation of this exact site pair. Compare primary host composition, alteration textures and fluid chemistry before computing overlap. The present release contains no paired assemblage measurements.

facts.text: Cerro Prieto research examined altered sediments near surface geothermal emissions.
Spirit found silica-rich materials near Home Plate.
Silica enrichment can have competing alteration explanations.

educational.whyItMatters: This comparison helps design a testable investigation. Best local process study, with historical Earth mineralogical observations and rover alteration evidence; the pair itself remains a proposed analogy.
educational.analogyBreakdown: Cerro Prieto is an active sediment-hosted geothermal system. Ancient Gusev alteration has competing interpretations; this is neither identical mineralogy nor a modern Mars environment. Earth has a protective atmosphere, a different radiation environment, abundant biology and different weathering. Gravity, atmospheric pressure and composition, liquid-water stability, thermal cycles and geological timescales differ. Infrastructure also changes terrestrial sites.

quiz.question: What does silica enrichment alone prove?
options: That microbes lived there
That the rock is identical to Cerro Prieto
Neither a unique formation mechanism nor life
That modern Mars has geothermal pools
quiz.explanation: Alternative reactions can enrich silica; independent context is needed.

experiment.title: Design an alteration transect
steps: Use permitted archived samples or published spectra; do not enter industrial geothermal areas.
Choose altered and background controls from the same host material.
Compare mineral identifications and record detection limits.
Test both leaching and precipitation hypotheses.
experiment.outcomeLabel: Educational scenario; not a real mission prediction
experiment.limitations: Cerro Prieto is an active sediment-hosted geothermal system. Ancient Gusev alteration has competing interpretations; this is neither identical mineralogy nor a modern Mars environment.

parameters.description: Case-sensitive record ID. When supplied, returns detail and bypasses pagination.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based page. Send digits with no leading zero.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Send digits with no leading zero.

Access-Control-Allow-Origin.description: Returned only when Origin matches STARMAN_ALLOWED_ORIGINS.

data.name: Mare Tranquillitatis basalt plains
data.coordinateSystem: Moon body-fixed geographic degrees; source convention recorded separately
data.coordinateRole: NASA regional marker, not a sample or Apollo landing coordinate
data.coordinateUncertainty: Regional display only; do not use for navigation or pixel extraction without product-label verification.

description.text: Lunar mare plains contain solidified basaltic lava.
